Grace —

Thanks — I am on this. Initial legal notes below; I attach a short redline with talking points (redline-notes.docx).

1) Contractual scope: we need the explicit Order Form and MSA version in effect for DC-4871. Look for any indemnity carveouts related to AI-generated outputs or third-party claims. Historically, Redwood MSA limits indemnity for claims arising from Customer-provided data but offers limited cover for model outputs only if certain usage thresholds/filters were enabled.

2) Key decision point: defend & control vs. indemnify under a reimbursement structure. If the Order Form ties indemnity to Customer content (vs. model defect), we may push responsibility to ClientCorp. If MSA language is ambiguous, we should evaluate the cost/risk tradeoffs and whether to offer a temporary credit for mitigation.

3) Evidence request: in addition to what Acme asked for, please include
- API request IDs and full JSON payloads
- Any post-processing or truncation applied to output
- Content moderation hit logs and timestamped human review notes (if any)
- Model weights/quantization identifier (model_hash) used at generation time

4) Timeline: Legal will draft an acknowledgement to Acme within 24 hours and a draft preservation letter for ClientCorp. We should schedule an internal triage call within 36 hours to assign owners.

Please prioritize locating the Order Form and a recent runbook for DC-4871. Ben — please confirm the ClientCorp contact info and whether they have a separate legal counsel to involve.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
